sub: One Cadence brain (cadence-net 0.91.1) playing Super Mario Bros. World 1-1 from the screen. One brain, trained once and kept learning, not a seed average.
seeing:
The real NES game, recorded frame by frame from the emulator while the brain played. Every button press in this clip was chosen by the Cadence brain: the lit keys under the screen are what it held for each 4-frame decision. No coach, planner or script is at the controls during this run. The bar under the keys is how far into the level Mario is (the flag is at the right).

The brain does not see the game the way you do. It gets a 26 x 32 grid of grey blocks (each block averages 8 x 8 pixels) for the present moment and for one decision ago, with the sky subtracted so only things light up. That is 1,664 numbers. It does not get Mario's position, the enemies' positions, or anything from the game's memory.
how:
1. Watch a coach. The coach is not a learner: at every moment it saves the emulator, tries 17 short button plans (run, run-jumps of different heights, wait, back off), and keeps the first button of whichever plan ends furthest right without dying. It clears 1-1 from every start we tried. The brain watched it play 20 times, some of them with deliberately wrong buttons mixed in so it also saw how to recover.
  2. Learn the screens. Each watched moment is one labelled screen. The brain learns them in shuffled lessons of 32 screens through Cadence's own local learning rule (equilibrium settling plus a nudge toward the shown button), at the library's teaching="normalized" point for imitation, with learning_surprise=True so it only studies the screens it still gets wrong. No backprop.
  3. Play, get corrected, repeat (DAgger). The brain plays on its own. Its own buttons are executed, so it reaches places the coach never went (like standing in front of a Goomba it should have jumped). The coach labels every screen the brain reached, the labels join the pile, and the same brain keeps learning. Some attempts start from a random point along the coach's path, so the brain also practises the later parts of the level. This is the recipe in Cadence's own teach guide.
  4. Test. After every round the brain plays alone from 5 fixed starts (0 to 23 idle frames before the first button, which shifts every Goomba's timing). That is the curve above.
doom: Sean heard someone made Cadence play Doom. What we found: Doom is on Cadence's official roadmap as issue #118, "Build and qualify the full native Doom expert", an open epic whose first skill is ViZDoom's Basic combat room, with only rendered screen information allowed into the player. We found no posted Cadence Doom results or public demo. The issue also says that a frame-to-action classifier taught by a host planner is a component control, not the full expert it is after. That is a fair description of this Mario demo too: it shows how far that component gets, nothing more.
